deep.reconstruction:
This folio (no. 94 in the bundle 600_2 notebook) has no calculations or derivations. Like the neighbouring pages 93 and 95, it is a run of aphorisms on the nature, method and philosophy of mathematics, separated by horizontal rules. The 'Gauss-Festschrift' named on p.93 is the Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899), so the entries are no earlier than 1899.

(1) Top fragment: '…sich unendlich kleine denken, sondern stets nur in solchen endlichen (beliebig grossen) Grenzen einschliessen, dass hernach beim Uebergang zu Null nichts Unvorhergesehenes passiren kann.' One should not imagine infinitely small quantities. Instead, one should always enclose quantities within finite bounds that may be taken arbitrarily large, so that nothing unforeseen can happen when passing to zero. In modern terms this is the Weierstrassian epsilon-delta (or epsilon-N) view of limits. A statement lim_{h->0} F(h) = L is replaced by: for every eps > 0 there is a delta > 0 such that |F(h) - L| < eps whenever 0 < |h| < delta. The finite bounds must be uniform, so that the limit passage is controlled (my gloss).

The sentence starts mid-thought and does not follow from the end of p.93 ('…Dampfbahn und Elektricität anwendet.'). It plausibly continues the last line of p.95: 'Unendlichklein ist = 0. Nicht klein auch nicht relativklein soll man sich der physika[lischen Grössen]…'. That suggests p.95 was written before the top of p.94, or that entries were made out of order (my inference).

(2) Mathematics needs few positive prior facts, but rather a certain mental gymnastics as preparatory training, which is not easy to go through. Arithmetic, algebra, analysis and function theory are only a theory of the four arithmetic operations. Geometry is nothing but a logical analysis and derivation of the facts of intuition (Anschauung). This states the arithmetisation programme for analysis and the Grundlagen der Geometrie view of geometry.

(3) A personal remark: speaking on general topics he does not fully master is unpleasant for him, so he does it only in extreme emergency.

(4) Detail work has value only if one keeps one's gaze on generality and on its use for knowledge of the foundations.

(5) Mathematics is a noble lady. She should neither beg from the neighbours (the other sciences) nor force herself on them, but she gladly grants her protection to those worthy of it.

(6) The mathematical limit (Grenze) is, in mathematics, what the Ideas are in life and philosophy (after Kant). The mathematical limit is the exact physical law, which exists only in us. We act as if it were exactly fixed; that is the simplest way and is necessary. This is the Kantian regulative idea and the 'als ob' stance applied to limits and exact physical laws. It anticipates Hilbert's 1925 'Über das Unendliche', where the infinite is given the role of a Kantian Idea.

(7) Start of a new aphorism, continued on p.95: one often hears complaints about mathematics from those who want to apply it. They demand that mathematics should spare them thinking or [make it superfluous…].

deep.surprise_reason: These are philosophical aphorisms, not results. The Kant-'Idee' comparison for the limit is a nice early (c.1900s) anticipation of the 1925 'Über das Unendliche' stance and of Vaihinger's 'als ob'. However, Hilbert's Kantian leanings are well known, so this is a modest documentary detail.
